name: Charlemagne
role: King of the Franks (768-814) and Emperor (800-814)
summary: Charlemagne expanded Frankish rule by conquest, incorporated the Lombard kingdom and subdued Saxony. His capitularies enforced Christian observance, directed religious education, required personal fidelity to the ruler and regulated access to grain in times of scarcity.

notes: The November 18 pass completed the current statement bank from the committed audit and checked earlier answers against the wording in force. It reviewed Einhard’s Life, the Royal Frankish Annals, the 789 Admonitio generalis, both Saxon capitularies, the 794 Frankfurt capitulary, the 802 general capitulary, the 806 Nijmegen and succession ordinances, the royal estate instructions, the 812 order concerning Hispani immigrants and letters to Baugulf and Michael I. The searches for the thinner themes covered famine and climate, livestock and forest rules, coinage, schooling, court procedure, marriage rules, military obligations, the Saxon campaigns and the peace negotiations with Byzantium. The 797 Saxon capitulary uses fines and local adjudication for some matters addressed under the earlier regime, with provisions for the king to demand higher fines in specified circumstances. Evidence was checked across economy, government, society, world affairs, liberty, culture, ecology, technology, means and globalism. The record is strongest on royal government, religious conformity, military expansion and relief during scarcity. Modern institutional questions and general policy claims beyond the scope of individual measures remain unknown.
